citation.title: Determination of plasma-ion velocity distribution via charge-exchange recombination spectroscopy
citation.authors: R. J. Fonck; D. S. Darrow; K. P. Jaehnig
citation.doi_or_arxiv: No DOI is printed in the supplied PDF. The APS pattern 10.1103/PhysRevA.29.3288 is unverified. DOIs in the reference list belong to cited works.

scope_read.limitations: The OCR is degraded on pp.3,5,9-10,12, and some equations and figure labels are partly illegible. The figures were read from captions and the legible text.

claim_checks.proposed_claim: Principle: beam-driven charge exchange excites impurity lines; Doppler width gives ion temperature and line shift gives bulk motion.
claim_checks.source_finding: Charge exchange with beam neutrals excites hydrogenic low-Z impurity lines. Viewing across the beam localizes the emission. The Doppler width gives Ti if non-thermal broadening is negligible, and the shift gives rotation.
claim_checks.locator: p.1 Sec.I; p.2 Eq.(1) and Sec.I; p.11 Sec.III Eq.(22)
claim_checks.allowed_intro_sentence: Charge-exchange recombination spectroscopy infers impurity-ion temperature and rotation from the Doppler width and shift of lines that beam neutrals excite at the beam-sightline intersection [Fonck1984].
claim_checks.qualification: This holds when Doppler broadening dominates. The quantity measured is the emitting impurity's velocity distribution.

claim_checks.proposed_claim: Atomic fine structure and l-mixing can distort line profiles and intensities.
claim_checks.source_finding: Unresolved fine structure widens the composite profile. The paper computes Ti correction factors that grow at low Ti and for low-n transitions (calculated for He+, C5+, O7+ at 25 keV/amu, field-free, Zeeman neglected). A simple model estimates ion-collision and motional-Stark l-mixing. This mixing mainly changes intensities, and the authors say it can shift the Ti correction by up to about 10%.
claim_checks.locator: p.11-12 Sec.III, Figs.12-15; p.6-9 Sec.II, Eqs.(5)-(21), Figs.7-11
claim_checks.allowed_intro_sentence: Reported CES temperatures depend on line-profile modelling, because unresolved fine structure and collisional l-mixing can alter apparent widths and intensities [Fonck1984].
claim_checks.qualification: These are model estimates, not measurements. The paper does not treat the KSTAR carbon line or its analysis chain.

claim_checks.proposed_claim: Ions created along the beam can drift into the sightline (plume) and delocalize the signal.
claim_checks.source_finding: Recombined ions that are electron-excited away from the intersection add beam-synchronous emission, so beam modulation cannot remove it. A 1-D model gives plume-to-prompt ratios that are largest for He+ and low beam energy and smaller for O VIII. Non-Gaussian He II wings were observed on PDX.
claim_checks.allowed_intro_sentence: Plume emission from beam-produced ions drifting along field lines can reduce the radial localization of CXRS signals, most strongly for very light impurities and low beam energies [Fonck1984].
claim_checks.qualification: The observation is for He II on PDX, and C5+ ratios are not plotted. Do not quantify a plume effect for KSTAR carbon CES.

input_target_timing.inputs: not_applicable: these are spectrometer line profiles of a diagnostic, not estimator inputs
input_target_timing.outputs: Ti and toroidal rotation from fitted Gaussians
input_target_timing.causal_or_offline: Offline least-squares fitting of spectral scans (p.18 Sec.V)
input_target_timing.reported_vs_physical_truth: Compared with passive-CX central Ti within error bars (p.18 Fig.23) and with TRANSP within 20% (p.20). This is consistency checking, not independent truth.

runtime_or_deployment.what_was_measured: Spectral-scan cadence: one scan every 50 ms with a scanning mirror (p.17 Sec.V), later every 20 ms with an optical multichannel analyzer (p.20 Sec.V)
runtime_or_deployment.what_not_established: Analysis latency, real-time processing, report arrival times

forbidden_inferences: These results apply to KSTAR carbon CES or provider chords
Plume or fine-structure magnitudes for our chord
Any statement about latency, nowcasting or causal estimation
Prior CXRS work was noncausal or electron-only
The 20/50 ms cadence is our report timing
competing_or_complementary: Complementary background physics only. It explains why the CES label is a model-dependent reported quantity, which supports treating labels as conventional rather than as truth. It neither competes with nor benchmarks temporal estimators.
